problem_text: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

ranking.title: Normal-bank-gated MIL: selecting abnormal instances by distance to normal source patches

Novelty.review: Weakly supervised lesion segmentation by MIL (FMaMIL) and medical anomaly segmentation against a normal feature memory (MIAS-SAM) both exist; using a normal-patch bank only to choose which patches MIL supervises in MVFA's segmentation adapters is a new combination rather than a new principle.

Feasibility.review: A coreset bank per source dataset and a detached gating term; training cost close to MVFA's. Bank construction adds a preprocessing step.

Clarity.review: Bank, gate, selection rule, hard negatives and baselines are specified; the bank level (level 4) for gating all four levels could be justified.

Impact.review: Directly answers the research problem and applies to all six BMAD modalities, including the unaligned ones.

Validity.review: Sound: normal anatomy has close neighbours in a normal bank while lesions do not; risk that rare normal variants are gated as lesion.

ranking.title: Mosaic MIL with normal-bank-gated instance selection

Novelty.review: No prior use of four-image mosaics to obtain free quadrant labels for weakly supervised anomaly localisation was found (mosaics are a detection augmentation); combined with gated MIL it is a new training signal.

Feasibility.review: Mosaic construction and gating are cheap; two mechanisms need joint tuning on source validation.

Clarity.review: Mosaic layout, quadrant labels, gating and losses are specified.

Impact.review: Spatially contrastive supervision without masks could substantially improve localisation from image labels.

Validity.review: Two mechanisms are combined, so attribution needs ablations, and quadrants at 120 px halve the resolution of small lesions.

ranking.title: Witness-rate-adaptive MIL: estimating each dataset's lesion fraction by positive-unlabelled mixture-proportion estimation
ranking.family: Witness rate and soft instance weighting

Novelty.review: Witness rate is a known MIL characteristic and class-prior estimation is standard in PU learning, but estimating it per dataset during training to set MVFA's MIL instance count is new for medical anomaly maps.

Feasibility.review: The estimator is cheap and runs every two epochs; no extra model.

Clarity.review: Estimator, update schedule, clipping and diagnostics are given.

Impact.review: Addresses a real flaw (fixed k across very different lesion sizes); the expected AUROC gain is moderate.

Validity.review: The best-bin estimator is principled when normal scores are a clean sample of the normal component; early-training scores may be uninformative, which the warm-up handles.

ranking.title: Mosaic MIL: free quadrant labels from four-image mosaics

Novelty.review: Free quadrant labels from mosaics of labelled images were not found in the weakly supervised anomaly-localisation literature; it creates spatial contrast that image-level MIL lacks.

Feasibility.review: Only a data wrapper and a loss term; no extra model or stage.

Clarity.review: Mosaic construction, labels, losses and the no-contrast ablation are clear.

Impact.review: If it works it is a general, cheap way to train localisation from image labels in medical imaging.

Validity.review: Down-scaling to 120 px quadrants weakens small-lesion evidence, and mosaic boundaries are artificial contexts the model may exploit.

ranking.title: Per-image adaptive k from normal-bank exceedances

Novelty.review: Per-image adaptive k from normal-bank exceedances is a sensible variant of witness-rate MIL; related ideas exist in memory-bank anomaly segmentation.

Feasibility.review: Requires a bank and a threshold per dataset; cheap during training.

Clarity.review: Threshold, clipping and selection are specified.

Impact.review: Improves instance count per image; moderate expected impact.

Validity.review: The 99th-percentile novelty threshold counts unusual normal anatomy as lesion, which could inflate k on exactly the images where anatomy misleads MIL.

Feasibility.review: Extra forward passes of four images per mosaic; manageable.

Impact.review: Mainly improves area calibration of maps; moderate impact.

Validity.review: Consistent maps across contexts are a reasonable requirement for anomaly maps; stop-gradient on single images avoids collapse.

ranking.title: Matched-pair MIL ranking: borrowing the ranking objective of weakly supervised video anomaly detection

Novelty.review: The MIL ranking loss is standard in weakly supervised video anomaly detection and MIL localisation exists in medical imaging; matched normal pairs by CLS similarity are a new twist.

Feasibility.review: Paired batches and precomputed neighbours; small changes.

Clarity.review: Loss, margin, pairing and the unmatched control are clear.

Impact.review: A relative objective could reduce anatomy-driven selections; moderate impact.

Validity.review: Matching on global similarity plausibly cancels shared anatomy; the unmatched control tests the mechanism.

ranking.title: Posterior-weighted MIL: a two-component mixture of patch scores replaces hard top-k selection
ranking.family: Witness rate and soft instance weighting

Novelty.review: Mixture-model posteriors as soft MIL targets are known in weak supervision; the per-dataset fit with a fixed normal component is a reasonable specialisation.

Feasibility.review: EM refits during training and kernel density estimates per dataset and level add engineering and tuning effort.

Clarity.review: Mixture, posterior, schedule and diagnostics are specified.

Impact.review: Soft targets could improve AUPRO moderately.

Validity.review: Gaussian lesion component and overlapping distributions early in training make posteriors unstable, as the follow-up idea acknowledges.

ranking.title: Co-teaching MIL between MVFA's detection and segmentation adapters

Novelty.review: Mutual distillation between two MIL learners exists (bi-directional MIL); using MVFA's detection and segmentation adapters as co-teaching partners is a method-specific application.

Feasibility.review: Uses existing branches; a few lines in the loss.

Clarity.review: Selection exchange, warm-up and weights are specified.

Validity.review: The two branches share backbone and data, so their errors may be correlated, which weakens the co-teaching rationale.

ranking.title: Feature-space anomaly mixing: graded synthetic positives from normal-bank patches

Novelty.review: Feature-level mixup is known; using it to create graded positives for anomaly-map adapters from normal-bank and likely-lesion features is a new use.

Feasibility.review: Cheap: mixing at adapter inputs within a batch.

Clarity.review: Mixing rule, soft targets and baselines are specified.

Impact.review: Could densify supervision; uncertain transfer to real lesions.

Validity.review: The assumption that a convex combination of features is abnormal in proportion lambda is weak for CLIP features, and the 'lesion' features come from MIL selections that may be anatomy.

Novelty.review: Multi-layer fusion of CLIP maps is common (LaRP-CLIP and others); using cross-level agreement as the MIL instance selector is a small, new twist.

Validity.review: Levels trained jointly may share errors, so agreement may not filter anatomy.

ranking.family: Witness rate and soft instance weighting

Novelty.review: An incremental refinement of posterior-weighted MIL.

Feasibility.review: Same refitting machinery as posterior MIL plus the MPE estimator.

Validity.review: Fixing the proportion stabilises EM but inherits the MPE estimator's bias.
